findings: THE AXIS SETTLES HALF THE BRANCH. Rothemund's odd-half-turn rule binds the distance between successive SCAFFOLD crossovers, which in a boustrophedon are the two ends of ONE ROW — an ALONG-helix length. So the width that moves is Gen1Tile.EDGE_X, 40.0 -> 38.08 nm, and the across-helix geometry is a COUNT of duplexes the scaffold never rasters along: 15 duplexes at 2.69 nm, 40.35 nm, unchanged. The root pitch, the plane lattice, the rise, C-0069's budget, C-0072's identity and C-0063's count vector all live on the along-helix lattice and carry no tile width, so they are invariant BY CONSTRUCTION.

THE BUILDABLE WIDTH SELECTS C-0063's OWN PHASE. 38.08 nm is 7 column pitches EXACTLY (40.0 nm is 7.35), so a column lands on the row end at the phases b = -56 (mod 16), i.e. 8 and 24 — and in a seamless boustrophedon that column IS the scaffold crossover that turns the raster. Those two phases are exactly C-0063's centro-symmetric pair, and 24 is its winner. C-0015's TEN eight-column phases collapse to these TWO (and to NONE if the row-end column is refused): the routing and the phase have stopped being independent choices.

THE BINDING ARM CEILING SWITCHES OWNER — on the rows whose outermost root sits at the PITCH, which on this lattice are the three-site rows. A three-arm row is bounded inboard by C-0069's pitch - d = 8.1900 nm and outboard by edgeX/2 - pitch, which is 9.1200 nm at 40.00 and 8.1600 nm at 38.08. The two cross at edgeX = 2(2p - d) = 38.1400 nm, and the buildable width falls 0.176 BASE PAIRS below that. So at 38.08 nm the tile edge binds where the plan budget used to, and C-0039's elastica arm — 8.16439083 nm, 24.0129 rises — overhangs by 0.004391 nm, which is 0.0129 of one rise.

AND THE LATTICE HOLDS THAT TOLERANCE AT ZERO. C-0085 has already established that a plan length is quantised at the rise; the elastica arm quantised down is 24 rises = 8.16 nm, and 32 bp of pitch plus 24 bp of arm is 56 bp, which is EXACTLY half of 112 bp. The outboard clearance is therefore 3.553e-15 nm — zero to machine precision — the three-arm row is restored, the phase-24 capacity goes 38 -> 45, and the whole centro-symmetric family (198288 placements at phase 24) is the SAME SET as at 40.00 nm. The buildable width does not merely tolerate C-0085's quantisation; it REQUIRES it.

THE TILE IS STILL FLAT. The best 34-root placement at 38.08 nm dishes 0.062147 of the stroke under C-0022's solved load, against T-5b's 0.10, the free tile's 0.2990 on the same host, and C-0063's 0.070615 at 40.00 nm. The station set is IDENTICAL at phases 8 and 24 (departure 0.0e+00 nm), so the whole difference is the HOST and the LOAD FIELD: what a 4.8 % narrower tile costs the flatness is -12.0 %.

C-0069's BUDGET IS TWO BOUNDS AND IT ONLY EVER REPORTED ONE. `pitch - d` is the INBOARD bound and carries no tile width; the OUTBOARD bound is `edgeX/2 - outermost root` and carries no interhelical distance. Bisected with C-0069's own library: on C-0063's own 34 rows the budget is 8.1900 -> 8.1900 nm, UNCHANGED, because all four of its three-arm rows sit on four-site rows whose outboard arm points inward anyway; on a three-site row carrying three arms it is 8.1900 -> 8.1600 nm, and there the tile edge owns it. C-0085's six-rise clearance loosens only the inboard bound, so on that row its widening goes 8.8400 -> 8.1600 nm and every clearance tighter than 8.00 rises now buys nothing. The razor follows as a CUBE: 2.34166 -> 2.31602 on the three-site row.

WHAT §3 HAS TO GIVE UP. Either the tile is 38.08 nm — 4.8 % narrower, 1537 nm2 instead of 1614, and §3's 100 pN over it is a 5.0 % higher pressure — or it carries a seam, which C-0081 prices at 6-12 of C-0063's 34 stations off the weave node and a worst across-row clearance of 0.122724 nm (-0.002276 at the measured girth, a clash). Both are SPECIFICATION consequences and neither is a modelling choice. The third rung, 144 bp = 48.96 nm, is 22 % LARGER and is not evaluated here.
